characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy controls the scope and credibility of demonstrator work across phases one through three. It establishes whether platform-neutral authentication is architecturally viable without exclusive reliance on Apple/Google integrity signals. Key deliverables include mobile-oriented demonstrators (FIDO2/WebAuthn on GrapheneOS or comparable platform) and browser-based or hardware-token fallback paths. Success metrics include working non-production prototypes, documented security assessments, and evidence that standards-based fallback mechanisms meet eIDAS2 'Substantial' assurance levels. This strategy directly underpins the project's credibility in policy and procurement engagement.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy strongly amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy by providing concrete evidence that platform-neutral alternatives are achievable. Demonstrators transform abstract feasibility arguments into tangible proof, increasing policy traction by approximately 15% and strengthening procurement negotiating positions. The strategy also enables Coalition Building Strategy by giving civil-society and academic partners credible technical artifacts to cite.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy creates resource and timeline trade-offs with Coalition Building Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy. Expanding demonstrator scope to include blockchain-anchored DIDs or multiple fallback pathways risks delaying phase-two delivery, which gates phase-three policy intervention and EU-level advocacy. Conversely, keeping demonstrator scope lean may limit the breadth of evidence available for broader standards conversations.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy translates technical and coalition work into formal proposals and regulatory engagement. It frames platform dependency as a resilience, continuity-of-service, and supplier-concentration problem rather than primarily a privacy issue, while maintaining accountability dimensions. Key objectives include securing written responses from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, influencing AltID design requirements, and aligning Danish positions with European Digital Identity Wallet standards. Success metrics are measured by formal institutional engagement, inclusion of platform-neutrality language in official procurement or policy documents, and demonstrated policy traction by month 24.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy amplifies Procurement Influence Strategy by establishing the regulatory narrative and institutional relationships necessary to embed platform-neutrality requirements into formal procurement documents. It also synergizes with EU Standards Engagement Strategy by demonstrating that Danish advocacy has institutional backing, lending credibility to EU-level standards arguments. Coalition Building Strategy strengthens advocacy reach by broadening the set of voices presenting aligned narratives to policymakers.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy faces tension with Coalition Building Strategy when coalition members hold conflicting priorities. Emphasizing continuity-of-service risk may alienate privacy-focused advocates, while foregrounding privacy and democratic accountability may reduce appeal to pragmatic procurement officials. Balancing these frames consumes political capital and may dilute the clarity of advocacy messaging.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy expands the project's political and institutional leverage by engaging civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, and sympathetic members of Folketinget's digital policy committee. It amplifies credibility and pressure across multiple constituencies. Key objectives include identifying lead partners in phase one, maintaining active stakeholder engagement through phases two and three, and consolidating coalition presence in procurement and standards discussions. Success metrics include documented stakeholder commitments, joint policy submissions, and demonstrated coalition participation in formal consultation processes.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Coalition Building Strategy directly amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy by providing multiple institutional voices for regulatory engagement and increasing advocacy credibility across government and public-sector bodies. It also strengthens Procurement Influence Strategy by enabling stakeholders to participate directly in procurement consultations and public comment periods. Coalition members provide technical credibility that supports Technical Feasibility Strategy uptake in policy discussions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Coalition Building Strategy creates coordination and messaging challenges when coalition members have competing priorities or institutional constraints. Recruiting dissenting voices from within MitID operator or Digitaliseringsstyrelsen may create internal conflicts that slow institutional engagement. Broader coalitions are harder to align, risking diluted messaging and reduced effectiveness in Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy negotiations.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy translates technical and policy work into formal requirements embedded in AltID procurement documents and related digital identity system specifications. It seeks to mandate platform-neutral access paths, certified fallback authentication mechanisms, and reduced exclusive dependence on Apple/Google infrastructure. Key objectives include securing inclusion of platform-neutrality and resilience language in official procurement documents, establishing fallback-access requirements, and influencing supplier evaluation criteria. Success metrics are measured by documented language changes in procurement specifications and evidence of supplier behavioral response to new requirements.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy directly amplifies Technical Feasibility Strategy by creating demand for the demonstrators and technical evidence the strategy produces. It synergizes with Policy Advocacy Strategy by translating policy proposals into binding procurement language. EU Standards Engagement Strategy supports procurement leverage by anchoring Danish requirements to broader European standards, making them appear less parochial and harder for incumbents to resist.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement Influence Strategy faces significant tension with Technical Feasibility Strategy regarding timeline. Procurement windows are constrained by institutional budgeting cycles; if demonstrators are not credible or ready by month 16, procurement influence becomes aspirational rather than actionable. It also conflicts with Coalition Building Strategy when procurement officials resist broad coalition input, preferring technical experts or incumbent vendors, thereby limiting the coalition's ability to shape requirements.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy positions Danish platform-neutrality advocacy within the broader European Digital Identity Wallet and eIDAS2 framework. It seeks to influence technical working groups, standards bodies, and EU-level policy discussions to incorporate platform-neutral access, certified fallback mechanisms, and reduced platform lock-in as European requirements. Key objectives include documented participation in relevant EU bodies, alignment of Danish positions with emerging European standards, and inclusion of platform-neutrality or resilience language in official European Digital Identity Wallet materials. Success metrics include evidence of Danish input in EU technical discussions and demonstrable influence on European standards trajectories.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy amplifies Procurement Influence Strategy by establishing that platform-neutrality is a European expectation, making it harder for Danish procurement officials to dismiss as parochial. It also strengthens Policy Advocacy Strategy by anchoring Danish proposals to EU-level regulatory momentum. Technical Feasibility Strategy demonstrators gain international credibility when presented as evidence supporting European standards discussions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy faces inherent tension with Procurement Influence Strategy regarding timelines and scope. EU standards development cycles are long; by the time European standards formally evolve, Danish AltID procurement may have already been finalized. There is also a resource conflict: meaningful EU engagement requires dedicated participation and political capital that may compete with the localized policy and procurement focus required in phase three.
